company_name: COSCO SHIPPING Energy Transportation Co., Ltd.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (minority partners in consolidated LNG vessel subsidiaries) at ~9x trailing NCI profit share, ~1.2x book
equity_bridge.note: Book RMB3,230.4m at 30 Jun 2026 (interim balance sheet); TTM NCI profit RMB422.7m. Group flows include the NCI share, so this is the single NCI charge.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run structural fleet growth (LNG/LPG newbuilds and VLCC renewal, offset by declining domestic coastal volumes) once the FY2026 tanker-rate peak has mean-reverted; the explicit 10-year path carries the cycle, this is the terminal rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 13.7% vs EPS 3yr CAGR 39.3% diverge by >30%: EPS is measured trough-to-peak across the tanker cycle (FY2022 RMB0.306 -> FY2025 RMB0.826) and parent equity was inflated by the Oct-2025 RMB8bn placement (ex-placement 3yr equity CAGR ~6.7%, 5yr ~2.1%). Neither CAGR is a usable forward growth rate for a cyclical; the scenario paths are built from the rate cycle and the orderbook instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip, net borrower): FY2018 -1,290; FY2019 3,955; FY2020 1,466; FY2021 410; FY2022 -320; FY2023 3,011; FY2024 710; FY2025 1,685 (RMB m). The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (negative FY2022 base) and the 5yr figure (2.8%) is noise: owner FCF has been swallowed by fleet growth capex (RMB4.4-7.9bn/yr) through the whole upcycle, and excludes RMB0.3-0.7bn/yr of JV/associate dividends booked in investing. Revenue CAGRs (3yr 8.5%, 5yr 7.8%) are cycle-inflated: FY2022 and FY2020 bases were both mid-cycle-or-better years, FY2025 was an upcycle year.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 is the peak of a VLCC supercycle (H1 2026 revenue +30%, EBITDA margin 57%, attributable profit +141%), not a new normal. Over FY2027-28 TD3C mean-reverts from >USD90k/day to the USD35-40k ten-year average as ~35 VLCCs deliver and the sanctions-driven tonne-mile windfall fades, taking revenue back to ~RMB25.5bn and the clean EBITDA margin to 41-42% (the FY2023-24 level). From FY2029 the RMB29.7bn newbuild programme -- 18 oil tankers, ~12 consolidated LNG carriers on long-term charters at USD70-80k/day, LPG/VLGC -- adds 3-4%/yr of volume, less the declining domestic coastal business, settling at 2.5% terminal growth. Net capex stays at RMB6-9bn/yr through FY2030 (commitments are contractual) then falls to fleet-replacement level (~20% of revenue, ~D&A). Terminal value is bounded by the 13x cyclical FCF cap, not Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supercycle extends through FY2027-28: EU/US sanctions on Russian and Iranian tonnage keep tightening, the compliant VLCC pool shrinks as the >20-year-old fleet scraps, the 2026-27 orderbook is absorbed by longer tonne-miles (India/Europe re-routing), and TD3C averages USD70k+ for two more years before normalising at a higher plateau. The consolidated LNG fleet grows ~40% on long-term charters and lifts the mid-cycle margin to 44%. Even on this path the current price is not reached: the market is capitalising peak earnings for longer than two years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle breaks in 2027: a Russia settlement and/or Iran sanctions relief releases shadow-fleet tonnage into compliant trade just as ~35 VLCC newbuilds deliver; TD3C falls below USD30k/day, domestic product-tanker volumes keep shrinking, LNG spot rates stay soft. Revenue falls to ~RMB21bn by FY2028 and the clean margin to 36% (FY2022: 35.7%). Committed newbuild capex is non-discretionary, so cash flow is squeezed when rates fall; a further equity raise or dividend cut becomes likely (not modelled).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the tanker cycle at mid-cycle, not at the FY2026 peak, and value the newbuild programme at what it costs as well as what it earns. The company's reported EBITDA margin went from -7% (FY2021) to 57% (H1 2026) in five years; carrying the latest margin forward would be a bet that the sanctions-driven VLCC supercycle is permanent. The driver paths therefore mean-revert revenue and margin to the FY2023-24 clean mid-cycle level by FY2028-29, charge the contractual RMB29.7bn of vessel commitments (plus H1 2026 spend, net of disposals) through FY2030, and only then let the fleet growth that capex buys show up as 3-4% volume growth. Terminal value is capped at 13x owner FCF (the cyclical range of the house method), the WACC is built in CNY and held identical across scenarios so cycle risk is charged once -- in the flows. At HKD18.37 the H share trades at ~9x annualised H1 2026 earnings and ~10x mid-cycle EV/EBITDA; the probability-weighted DCF value sits well below that, and so does the bull case. The finding is that the market is pricing a multi-year supercycle, not a 2026 peak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment (41% base): each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly RMB0.3-0.4/share; FY2022's 35.7% and FY2024's 42.8% bracket the plausible range
Cycle duration: if TD3C holds above USD70k/day through FY2028 (bull), cumulative FY2026-28 owner FCF roughly doubles versus base

Capex programme: the path assumes no orders beyond the RMB29.7bn committed at Jun 2026; the commitments grew RMB11bn in six months, and further ordering at peak-cycle newbuild prices would lower value (and could trigger another equity raise)

Sanctions regime is the bull and the bear: tightening keeps the compliant-fleet premium; relief (Russia/Iran) collapses it; a repeat of the 2019 OFAC designation of a COSCO subsidiary would cut charterer demand for the Group's own tonnage
FX: all values are CNY converted at CNY/HKD 1.1728; a 5% RMB move is a 5% move in the HKD values; USD-linked freight revenue against RMB costs also moves the margin
NCI valued at RMB3.8bn (~9x profit share); valuing it at book (RMB3.2bn) adds ~RMB0.10/share, at 12x subtracts ~RMB0.25/share
Terminal cap at 13x FCF (~5.5x mid-cycle EBITDA) is below where listed LNG carrier owners trade (~9-10x EBITDA) and in line with tanker peers (6-8x); a 15x cap raises base value ~10%

inputs.share_count_basis: 5,471.207m shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 2026 interim, balance sheet) plus 7.876m treasury-method dilutive effect of the 19.16m share options outstanding (interim note 10(2), 36). Held FLAT: SBC (0.3% of revenue) is expensed in the flows. The Oct-2025 RMB8bn A-share placement (694m shares at RMB11.52) is already in the count; no further non-SBC issuance is modelled in the base, though the RMB29.7bn newbuild commitments make a further raise a bear-case risk (noted, not modelled).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, cash-flow reconciliation note 38(a) 'Share-based payment expense 68,936' (RMB'000) -> RMB68.9m; H1 2026 interim RMB26.3m. No equity-award cash taxes disclosed (net-share settlement is not used; options are exercised for cash, RMB73.1m proceeds in H1 2026).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H shares quoted in HKD on HKEX. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted at CNY/HKD 1.1728 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16; 1 CNY = 1.1728 HKD). Parity check against the Shanghai A-share dual listing 600026.SS at CNY 20.55 (2026-10-16): the H share at HKD 18.37 = CNY 15.66, i.e. a 23.8% A/H discount, inside the 20-40% band the H share has historically traded at versus the A share -- the direction and quote basis tie; the A/H discount itself is a market feature, not an FX error. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-check the rate on any later price refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T03:59:43Z (HKEX morning-session print, intraday; afternoon session still to trade -- replace at the regular close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8%, equity risk premium 6.5% (China/HK), beta 1.3 (listed tanker owners run empirically high betas; this is systematic risk, not a cyclicality premium -- cycle risk is charged in the scenario paths, not here) -> cost of equity 10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt 3.4% (H1 2026 interest on bank/other borrowings RMB622m annualised against ~RMB37bn average borrowings, SOFR-linked USD plus RMB bank debt and the RMB2.5bn bond), ~3.0% after tax. Market-value weights at the current price: equity RMB85.8bn, debt RMB38.7bn -> D/V 31%, rounded to 30/70. WACC = 0.7 x 10.2 + 0.3 x 3.0 = 8.0%, held identical across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities RMB1,046.6m (454.1 non-current + 592.5 current, 30 Jun 2026) are inside total_debt -- which is the company's own 'total debts' figure of RMB38,693.7m (interest-bearing bank and other borrowings 33,024.3 + other loans 2,117.4 + bond 2,505.4 + leases 1,046.6). Lease principal (RMB375m H1 2026) is NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use depreciation (~RMB540m/yr) stays inside the D&A path and its renewal is carried in the capex path (~2% of revenue). Charter-in hire for time charters is an operating cost already inside EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (chiefly minority partners in consolidated LNG vessel-owning subsidiaries) are deducted ONCE, in the equity bridge, at RMB3,800m: trailing-12-month NCI profit share RMB422.7m (FY2025 385.8 - H1 2025 199.1 + H1 2026 236.0) at ~9x, i.e. ~1.2x the RMB3,230.4m book value at 30 Jun 2026. The flows are therefore GROUP flows (including the NCI share), which is why the FY0 NOPAT calibration is against total profit (RMB4,422.9m FY2025) rather than attributable (RMB4,037.1m). Not deducted: the RMB1,531m financial guarantee to CSLNG joint ventures (contingent, performing).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical/non-US adaptations (dual currency, CNY WACC, leases-as-debt, NCI in bridge, mid-cycle normalisation, 13x cyclical terminal cap). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'; first valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). WHY NOT A FLAT-MARGIN DCF: H1 2026 (revenue +30%, EBITDA margin 57.4%, attributable profit +140.6%) is a VLCC supercycle print; FY2021 was an EBITDA loss. The driver paths deliberately take FY2026 as the cycle peak and mean-revert revenue and margin to the FY2024-type mid-cycle (TD3C ~USD35-40k/day, clean EBITDA margin ~41%) by FY2028-29, with structural volume growth thereafter from the LNG/LPG/VLCC newbuild programme. EBITDA DEFINITION: the company's EBITDA (PBT + finance costs + D&A) includes share of JV/associate profits (RMB774m JV + associates in FY2025, mainly the 50%-owned CLNG LNG fleet), disposal gains (RMB669m FY2025) and interest income (RMB171m). The margin path is anchored to a CLEAN margin (ex disposal gains, impairments, interest income) but KEEPS the JV/associate share in the flows, because their cash dividends (RMB726m FY2025) are real and recurring; consequently investments in JVs/associates are NOT added in the bridge (matching-asset rule, charged once). Note that reported_fcf (OCF - PPE purchases) EXCLUDES those JV/associate dividends, which sit in investing activities, so last_fcf understates owner cash generation by ~RMB0.7bn in FY2025 -- the forward build does not inherit that understatement. INTEREST INCOME: the company is a net borrower (net debt RMB20.5bn), so no interest-income strip is applied; the ~0.7%-of-revenue interest income is inside the historical margins and immaterial. CAPEX: the path is NET of vessel disposal proceeds (RMB1,925m FY2025; 20 tankers, 1.77m DWT scheduled for disposal in 2026) and is sized to absorb the RMB29,670m vessel commitments due 2026-2030 (interim note 33) plus the RMB5,782m already spent in H1 2026, with no allowance for further orders; FY2031+ capex ~20% of revenue, i.e. roughly equal to D&A, which is fleet-replacement steady state. TAX: PRC statutory 25% but international shipping income is largely earned through HK/offshore subsidiaries at low rates; cash tax / EBIT was 11.4% FY2025, 11.2% FY2024, 14.4% FY2023; the H1 2026 expense rate on PBT was 19%. A flat 14% cash rate on EBIT is used -- modestly above the cash history. BUYBACKS: none in the history (dividends only; payout ~25-50% of attributable profit). SBC-NEAR-ZERO: SBC is 0.3% of revenue, so house and street bases almost coincide; the band_position the engine reports is degenerate and should be read as 'not meaningful' -- the current price sits far outside a band that is only ~HKD0.3 wide. BAND OF VALUE: at HKD18.37 the market capitalises roughly the H1 2026 annualised earnings (~9x peak P/E, ~6.5x FY2026E EV/EBITDA, ~10x mid-cycle EV/EBITDA); the DCF says that price is only reached if the supercycle persists for several years beyond FY2026 -- it lies above even the bull case.
inputs.ebitda_history_note: Company EBITDA (RMB m) / revenue / margin: FY2018 3,884 / 12,100 / 32.1%; FY2019 5,295 / 13,721 / 38.6%; FY2020 6,948 / 16,268 / 42.7%; FY2021 -860 / 12,645 / -6.8%; FY2022 6,630 / 18,567 / 35.7%; FY2023 9,350 / 21,912 / 42.7%; FY2024 10,219 / 23,133 / 44.2%; FY2025 10,613 / 23,701 / 44.8%; H1 2026 8,660 / 15,079 / 57.4%. Clean of disposal gains, impairments and interest income: FY2024 ~42.8%, FY2025 ~43.1%. Segment FY2025 gross margins: oil shipping 23.0% (international 22.3%, domestic 24.8%), LNG 49.3%, LPG 28.2%, chemical 14.4%; LNG is 10.7% of revenue and growing (24 LNG carriers under construction against 63 in operation, ~half via the 50% JV).

bear.narrative: The cycle breaks in 2027: a Russia settlement and/or Iran sanctions relief releases shadow-fleet tonnage into compliant trade just as ~35 VLCC newbuilds deliver; TD3C falls below USD30k/day (the FY2021-22 experience), domestic product-tanker volumes keep shrinking, and LNG spot rates stay soft under 85 industry deliveries. Revenue falls back to ~RMB21bn by FY2028 and the clean margin to 36%, close to FY2022's 35.7%. Committed newbuild capex (RMB29.7bn) is non-discretionary, so cash flow is squeezed hardest exactly when rates fall; a further equity raise or dividend cut becomes likely (not modelled). The RMB-denominated capex path is held slightly higher than base (unchanged commitments on a smaller revenue base).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +24.5% to ~RMB29.5bn: H1 2026 actual RMB15.08bn (+30%) plus an H2 slightly below the Q2 run-rate (RMB7.8bn/qtr) as 20 older tankers are disposed; management's RMB23.17bn plan is already obsolete. FY2027 -8% and FY2028 -6%: VLCC TD3C mean-reverts from >USD90k/day toward the ~USD35-40k 10-year average as ~35 VLCC newbuilds deliver and sanctions-driven tonne-mile gains fade, partly cushioned by LNG deliveries (10 in 2026) and firm long-term LNG charter rates (USD70-80k/day). FY2029-32 +3-4%: the RMB29.7bn newbuild programme (18 oil tankers 2.96m DWT, ~12 consolidated LNG carriers, LPG/VLGC) lands, less the declining domestic coastal segment. FY2033-35 +2.5% to terminal.
base.margin_rationale: 55% FY2026 (H1 actual 57.4%, H2 a little softer), 48% FY2027, then 41-42% -- the clean FY2023-24 mid-cycle level (42.8% FY2024 at TD3C ~USD35k/day ex disposal gains and interest income), held rather than raised despite the rising LNG mix because the domestic coastal and product-tanker segments are in structural decline and FY2022 printed 35.7%.
base.capex_rationale: Net of disposal proceeds. FY2026 30.5% (~RMB9.0bn: H1 actual RMB5.8bn gross, 20 tanker disposals offsetting part of H2), FY2027 27.5% (~RMB7.5bn), FY2028 25.5% (~RMB6.5bn), FY2029 23% (~RMB6.0bn), FY2030 21% (~RMB5.7bn): FY2026-30 total ~RMB34.7bn against RMB29.7bn commitments (Jun 2026) + RMB5.8bn H1 2026 spend, i.e. no new orders assumed. FY2031+ 20% ~ D&A, fleet replacement steady state.
base.da_rationale: FY2025 D&A RMB3,914m = 16.5% of revenue; H1 2026 RMB2,109m. Newbuild deliveries add ~RMB1.2bn/yr by FY2030 (RMB29.7bn over ~25-year lives), taking D&A to ~RMB5.5bn ~20% of mid-cycle revenue; the FY2026 ratio is low only because the denominator is peak revenue.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax / EBIT: 11.4% FY2025, 11.2% FY2024, 14.4% FY2023 (HK/offshore international shipping income at low rates, PRC 25% on domestic). 14% flat is modestly above the cash history; the engine never credits tax on a loss.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables and bunker inventories grow with revenue; -5% of the change in revenue consumes cash in growth years and releases it in FY2027-28 as revenue falls.

bull.narrative: Supercycle extends through FY2027-28: EU/US sanctions on Russian and Iranian tonnage keep tightening, the compliant VLCC pool shrinks as the >20-year-old fleet scraps, the 2026-27 VLCC orderbook is absorbed by longer tonne-miles (India/Europe re-routing), and TD3C averages USD70k+ for two more years before normalising at a higher plateau. The consolidated LNG fleet grows ~40% on long-term charters at USD70-80k/day and lifts the mid-cycle margin to 44%. Even here the price is not reached.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. The default bull tilt is for quality compounders; this is a price-taking cyclical valued at a rate peak, where the two tails are genuinely symmetric and both political: the bull needs sanctions on Russian/Iranian tonnage to persist AND the 2026-27 VLCC orderbook to be absorbed; the bear is a single event (sanctions relief) coinciding with those deliveries while RMB29.7bn of capex is contractually committed. Bear is held at 25% rather than higher because the balance sheet was de-risked by the Oct-2025 RMB8bn placement (net gearing 77% -> 40%, cash RMB18.2bn) and ~11% of revenue is long-term-contracted LNG, so the downside is an earnings cycle, not a solvency event.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
